svg.title: First actions for a Victorian bush emergency
svg.desc: Working three-part bush-emergency routing card. Part one says that immediate danger, obvious life-threatening bleeding, an unresponsive person who is not breathing normally, or another serious illness or injury overrides the overview and routes immediately to Triple Zero and the matching Chapter 6 action. Gasping or uncertain breathing counts as not breathing normally. The card does not resolve simultaneous life threats for a lone rescuer. Part two says to stop unnecessary movement, keep the group together when safe, call Triple Zero without waiting for perfect coordinates or complete notes, and continue urgent care and protection while using Chapter 3 if the call fails. It does not authorise climbing or wandering for signal. Part three says to stay near the reported place unless it becomes unsafe or responders direct movement, improve protection near the safe waiting place, record known and unknown facts, stay findable and recheck whenever something changes. Rescue delay is not permission for an unplanned walkout. The card teaches no CPR, bleeding-control, device-operation, location-fixing, movement, shelter or signalling technique.
svg.text: FIRST ACTIONS — DANGER + LIFE THREATS
WORKING CARD · PART 1 OF 3
WARNING — ROUTING CARD; SPECIALIST REVIEW NEEDED
Estimates: core wording 95%; combined ordering 75%; new layout 60%.
These do not estimate safety, contact, rescue, treatment or survival.
No fixed order overrides immediate danger or a critical injury.
Do not finish this card before urgent care. Follow 000 and the matching card.
IMMEDIATE DANGER OR UNSURE?
Do not enter or remain exposed to read this card.
Move only as far as needed to reduce the threat. Call 000 from safety.
Every further movement decision belongs to Chapter 4.
EITHER BOX IS AN IMMEDIATE EXIT — NOT A SEQUENCE
OBVIOUS LIFE-THREATENING
BLEEDING?
Call 000. Use the Chapter 6
severe-bleeding card now.
Do not finish this overview first.
UNRESPONSIVE + NOT
BREATHING NORMALLY?
Gasping or unsure counts. Call 000.
Use the Chapter 6 CPR/AED cards.
Do not finish this overview first.
OTHER SERIOUS ILLNESS OR INJURY? Call 000; use the matching Chapter 6 action.
Competing tasks? Capable helpers act in parallel; no lone-rescuer priority is set here.
With or without a kit, do not delay urgent care while searching for equipment.
NO IMMEDIATE OVERRIDE? CONTINUE TO PART 2
STOP — KEEP TOGETHER — GET HELP
WORKING CARD · PART 2 OF 3
PART 1 STILL CONTROLS
Urgent care and the 000 call can happen together when a capable helper is
available. Never pause the matching emergency card to finish this overview.
STOP UNNECESSARY MOVEMENT
Stop and bring the group within speaking distance only when safe.
Keep the group together. Do not split up or send a messenger.
Use Chapter 4 for every stay, move, retrace or missing-person decision.
URGENT RESCUE OR MEDICAL EMERGENCY? CALL 000
Unable to find your way back and need rescue help? Ask for Police.
Serious illness or injury? Ask for Ambulance. Describe every problem that applies.
Do not wait for perfect coordinates, a complete note or a full inventory.
State what is known and uncertain. Use Chapter 3 now.
000 DID NOT CONNECT?
Keep urgent care and protection going. Use Chapter 3's failed-contact branches.
Do not climb, wander or leave the person merely to seek signal.
If the site becomes unsafe, move only the minimum needed; then report the change.
WORKING DRAFT — CONTINUE TO PART 3
PROTECT — RECORD — RECHECK
WORKING CARD · PART 3 OF 3
URGENT CARE + FIRST HELP ATTEMPT UNDERWAY?
If no, return to Parts 1–2. Keep essential care and contact going.
Follow live responder directions over this card. Never use this part alone.
PROTECT PEOPLE · STAY FINDABLE
Stay near the reported place unless it becomes unsafe or responders direct a move.
Keep the group together. Improve protection from weather and cold ground nearby.
Make the position visible only without entering danger or abandoning care.
Use Chapters 4 and 5. This card gives no movement, shelter or signalling method.
WRITE WHAT IS KNOWN — MARK WHAT IS UNKNOWN
PEOPLE · POSITION + UNCERTAINTY · TIME · PROTECTION
SUPPLIES · CONTACT ATTEMPTS / REPLIES · CHANGES
Do not guess. Unknown never means safe. Use Chapter 9 for position details.
Urgent care and the first help attempt always come before notes.
RECHECK WHENEVER SOMETHING CHANGES
People: response, normal breathing, bleeding, temperature, other deterioration.
Situation: danger, weather, protection, contact and responder directions.
Change? Return to Part 1 or the matching card. No rescue deadline or walkout.
NOT FIELD-APPROVED · USE ALL PARTS WITH THE CHAPTER WARNING
